Q: How to use images when it comes to SQL databases? A:

Question #1: How to store image in a MySQL table

MySQL supports blob data types, allowing you to store images or any other kind of binary data. There are 4 such types which only vary in sizes:

  • TINYBLOB : up to 255 bytes, best for keeping very tiny icons or flags
  • BLOB : up 64 KB, for things like small GIF/JPEG images, normal size documents
  • MEDIUMBLOB : up to 16 MB, enough to keep most PDF files and photo images or music MP3s
  • LONGBLOB : up to 4 GB, should be enough to hold videos

So far there's no larger blob type available in MySQL yet.

See also:

  • https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/blob.html
  • https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/storage-requirements.html

Store image to blob column

To create a table with a blob column enough to keep a normal size image:

CREATE TABLE data_table (
  id   INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, -- eg. 'family-gathering.jpg'
  mime VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,  -- eg. 'image/jpeg'
  data MEDIUMBLOB NOT NULL
);

If your image is already stored in a location where DB server can directly access to, this is the statement to store the image data into DB:

INSERT INTO data_table(name, mime, data)
VALUES('family-gathering.jpg', 'image/jpg', LOAD_FILE('/path-to-the-file/family-gathering.jpg'));

But oftentimes that is not the case and the data is actually only available on the application server, not DB server. You can pass the data just like ordinary column data in your SQL query. The following is a possible example code written in C#:

using System.IO;
using MySql.Data.MySqlClient;

// prepare variables host, db, account, db, dirPath, fileName...

byte[] data = File.ReadAllBytes($"{dirPath}/{fileName}");
using (var conn = new MySqlConnection($"Server={host};Database={db};User ID={account};Password={pw};"))
{
    conn.Open();
    string sql = """
                 INSERT INTO data_table(name, mime, data)
                 VALUES (@name, @mime, @data)
                 """;
    using var cmd = new MySqlCommand(sql, conn);
    cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@name", fileName);
    cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@mime", "image/jpg");
    cmd.Parameters.Add("@data", MySqlDbType.MediumBlob).Value = data;
    cmd.ExecuteNonQuery();
}

Retrieve image from blob column

Just like any other types of data, like so:

SELECT name, mime, data
FROM data_table
WHERE id = 1234;

Or if you want to store it on certain location in DB server:

SELECT data
INTO DUMPFILE '/path-to-the-output-file/saved-family-gathering.jpg'
FROM data_table
WHERE id = 1234;

As explained in:

  • https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/select-into.html

But generally this is not the preferred solution, not only it saves the data on DB server, it's also saved with a fixed name in certain directory path. And currently due to MySQL's limitation we cannot use a variable in the INTO DUMPFILE clause. That means in a multi-user DB server it is highly likely to have a collision probllem.

The preferred way is to use the ordinary SELECT without INTO DUMPFILE and the application code should receive the blob data and store it on application side.

Question #2: Store image on an external storage

It is quite common practice to store large data files, such as images, outside of a database server. DB servers are not the most efficient storage solution for such task. Instead, you can use a service specifically designed for the purpose and AWS S3 is one such option. However, be prepared that cloud storage services would charge for storage fees one way or another.

If you decide to go this route, you need to design the table columns to store the image's identity info such as the resource path on the storage service and the resource ID. Also the storage service typically would require an authentication key or token so your application can access the data. It is strongly recommended not to keep this authentication info in DB to avoid potential security risks. Instead, your program should be designed so that the authentication credentials are retrieved from a secure source or obtained dynamically from the storage service as a one‑time access key or token.

Q: Recommendations for an API to integrate licensing into my app A:

I work on Keymint , a licensing API that might fit your needs. It lets you issue license keys, bind them to a specific machine (node-locking), and supports free keys for selected individuals. You can also create volume licenses with activation limits if you need that later. It has a free tier for up to 25 licenses, which could work for testing. The API is straightforward: you create a key, the user enters it in your app, and you call the activation endpoint with a host ID. There are SDKs for Node, Python, Go, and C#. Might be worth a look.

Q: How to remove contours with opencv? A:

Here is one way in Python OpenCV.

  • Read the input

  • Convert to grayscale

  • Threshold and invert

  • Get all contours

  • Filter contours on area

  • Sort filtered contours in increasing area

  • Remove successive contours keeping the smallest if the areas are too close in size

  • Draw contours as white on a black background

  • Get the rotated rectangles for the remaining contours

  • Draw these contours as red on copy of the input

  • Draw these contours as black on a white background

  • Save the images

Input:

import cv2
import numpy as np

# read the input
img = cv2.imread('box_text.png')

# convert to grayscale
gray = cv2.cvtColor(img,cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

# threshold and invert
thresh = cv2.threshold(gray, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY_INV+cv2.THRESH_OTSU)[1]

# get all contours
contours = cv2.findContours(thresh, cv2.RETR_TREE, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
contours = contours[0] if len(contours) == 2 else contours[1]

#  filter contours to get contours larger in area than a threshold 
area_threshold = 14000
filt_contours = [cntr for cntr in contours if cv2.contourArea(cntr) > area_threshold]

# draw contours as white on a black background
cntr_img1 = np.zeros_like(thresh)
cv2.drawContours(cntr_img1, filt_contours, -1, (255), 2)

# sort contours in increasing area in order to keep the smaller of two close contours
sorted_contours = sorted(filt_contours, key=cv2.contourArea, reverse=False)

# remove successive contours that are too close in area
filt_cntrs = []
area_diff_percent = 20
for cntr in sorted_contours:
  current_area = cv2.contourArea(cntr)

  if not filt_cntrs or len(filt_cntrs) == 1:
    # keep the first two contours, since smallest two contours are too close for thresholding
    filt_cntrs.append(cntr)
  else:
    # get the previous kept contour's area
    previous_kept_area = cv2.contourArea(filt_cntrs[-1])

    # check if differences in area are greater than some threshold
    if 100 * abs(previous_kept_area - current_area) / previous_kept_area > area_diff_percent:
      filt_cntrs.append(cntr)
print(len(filt_cntrs))

# draw contours as white on a black background
cntr_img2 = np.zeros_like(thresh)
cv2.drawContours(cntr_img2, filt_cntrs, -1, (255), 2)

# get rotated rectangles and draw on copy of input and as black on white background
rotrect_img = img.copy()
rectangles_img = np.full_like(thresh, 255)
for cntr in filt_cntrs:
    # get rotated rectangle from contour
    rot_rect = cv2.minAreaRect(cntr)
    box = cv2.boxPoints(rot_rect)
    box = np.int32(box)
    # draw rotated rectangle on copy of img
    cv2.drawContours(rotrect_img,[box],0,(0,0,255),5)
    cv2.drawContours(rectangles_img,[box],0,(0),5)


# save images
cv2.imwrite('box_text_thresh.jpg', thresh)
cv2.imwrite('box_text_contours_area_filtered.jpg', cntr_img1)
cv2.imwrite('box_text_contours_successive_filtered.jpg', cntr_img2)
cv2.imwrite('box_text_rectangles_on_image.jpg', rotrect_img)
cv2.imwrite('box_text_rectangles.jpg', rectangles_img)


# show images
cv2.imshow('thresh', thresh)
cv2.imshow('contours_area_filtered', cntr_img1)
cv2.imshow('contours_successive_filtered', cntr_img2)
cv2.imshow('rectangles on image', rotrect_img)
cv2.imshow('rectangles', rectangles_img)
cv2.waitKey(0)
